scenes.heading: UNSLOP: EVERY AI SCREEN
scenes.say: You've seen this screen. Why does every AI-built app look the same?

scenes.heading: FIRST, IT NAMES THE SLOP
scenes.say: unslop is a skill for Claude Code or Codex, and it starts by naming the slop out loud, and where it lives.

scenes.heading: YOUR ANSWER IS THE DIRECTION
scenes.say: Then it asks what your product actually is. Your answer becomes the direction: the character, the one moment that carries the colour, the signature detail.

scenes.heading: NINE PASSES, ONE SCREEN
scenes.say: Then it redraws the same screen in nine passes, so what you get back still looks like your product, just designed.

scenes.heading: TYPE SLASH UNSLOP
scenes.say: Type slash unslop, then your screen or a live link. It runs in Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte or plain CSS.

scenes.heading: SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT PRODUCT
scenes.say: Same layout, same words, different product. That is the whole point.

scenes.heading: WHAT TO EXPECT
scenes.say: If your screen is already good it says so; it asks before any paid image; and it needs Claude Code or Codex to run.

idea: unslop names the slop in an AI-looking screen, takes a direction from the product, and redraws the same screen in nine passes.

claims.text: unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that finds the slop in a screen and names it, with where it lives, before it edits anything.
It proposes a direction taken from the product — character, the moment that carries the colour, a signature detail — and you steer it before it edits anything.
It then fixes the screen in nine passes — spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion — in that order, on the same screen.
You run it by typing /unslop with your screen or a live link, and it works in whatever the screen is built with.
The result keeps the layout and the words of the screen it was given; what changes is the product it now looks like.
